newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chairman makes offer for China Strategic.
newsitem.headline: Chairman makes offer for China Strategic.

text.p: China Strategic Holdings Ltd chairman Oei Hong Leong has made a general offer for all shares in the company which he does not hold, the company said in a notice published on Thursday.
Oei is offering shareholders HK$2.50 per share and HK$0.01 per warrant, the notice said.
The shares, which were suspended from trading on Wednesday, closed on Tuesday at HK$2.375, and the warrants at HK$0.29.
Trading in the shares will be resumed on Thursday.

Oei and parties acting in concert with him raised their stake in the company on Wednesday above the 35 percent trigger point -- the level at which a general offer for all publicly held shares must be made -- through the exercise of share options granted under the company's Executive Share Option Scheme adopted on July 20, 1992, the notice said.

The exercise of the options by Oei, Sanion Enterprises Ltd, a private company beneficially owned by Oei, and other parties acting in concert with Oei, brought the shareholding of the chairman's group to 35.76 percent from 34.66 percent.

"The offer price of HK$2.50 per share is equal to the highest price paid by the offeror (Oei and others) of HK$2.50 per share within the six months preceding October 9, 1996, and represents a premium of approximately 5.26 percent over the closing price of HK$2.375 per share as quoted...on October 8," the notice said.
The offer price also represents a discount of approximately 16.94 percent to the audited net asset value of HK$3.01 per share, as at the last balance sheet date of December 31, 1995, it said.

The share offer and warrant offer value the entire issued share capital of the company at HK$1.62 billion and the total consideration payable by the chairman's group to shareholders at HK$767.56 million, the notice said..
The offer excludes a HK$170.53 million convertible note held by a Hutchison Whampoa subsidiary and exercisable into 117.27 million shares.
Those shares would represent 18.15 percent of the current share capital of the company or 17.75 percent of its enlarged issued share capital following the conversion, it said.
